bugs.summary: A wikilink's end offset stops one byte short of the closing ]], so into_offset_iter reports a truncated span.
bugs.match_rule: Names the wikilink node's end offset being set to end_ix + 1 although end_ix is the start of the two-byte closing ]], so the reported source range omits the final bracket.
bugs.caveat: The candidate also said later text overlaps; not observed, the following text stays at 43..44. Only the short span is claimed. Needs ENABLE_WIKILINKS.

bugs.summary: A piped wikilink with its child reused from the tree keeps that node's next chain, so later content is visited as both child and sibling and events double per link.
bugs.match_rule: Names exponential event growth from handle_wikilink's piped or pothole path, where a reused tree node becomes the wikilink's child without its next chain being cut at the closing delimiter, so following content is reachable twice.
bugs.caveat: Events are capped with take(), so memory exhaustion itself was not run; the curve is event count. Needs ENABLE_WIKILINKS.

bugs.summary: A tab-indented definition start subtracts a column count from a byte offset, so into_offset_iter returns ranges inside a multibyte character.
bugs.match_rule: Names the definition-list definition node's start computed as container_start - outer_indent, where outer_indent is in columns (tabs expand) but the start is a byte offset, so source ranges can be wrong or fall inside a character.
bugs.caveat: The panic is in the caller's slice, not the parser, so the kind stays wrong-behavior. Lines 131 and 133 have a similar subtraction for lists, fixed separately in 3cbeeec6; a finding only about lists does not match. Needs ENABLE_DEFINITION_LIST.

bugs.summary: handle_wikilink computes end_ix - start_ix and slices start_ix..end_ix without checking order, so malformed image wikilink input panics.
bugs.match_rule: Names a panic in handle_wikilink where the body start can be past the closing delimiter, causing the end_ix - start_ix underflow or the inverted block_text slice. Either site counts.
bugs.caveat: Needs ENABLE_WIKILINKS. The issue's U+FFFD prefix and Options::all() are not needed.

bugs.summary: With default options, a list item holding only a link reference definition followed by a whitespace-only line leaves an empty TightParagraph, and the parser unwraps its missing child.
bugs.match_rule: Names a reachable panic from an empty TightParagraph, at self.tree.cur().unwrap() in Parser::next or OffsetIter::next, or names the link reference definition title scan treating a following whitespace-only line as a continuation so that the paragraph ends up with no children.
bugs.caveat:
This is the only crash needing no options. The bug was added by 4409722 (2025-02-10), before the tag. The fix commit's message and tests describe a spurious
, not this panic; the link rests on the control above and upstream's #1129 comment 'Fixed by #1021'. Added while building the key, not in the original candidates.

bugs.summary: HTML block end tags match case-sensitively, so <script> closed by </SCRIPT> never ends and following Markdown becomes raw HTML.
bugs.match_rule: Names the HTML block end-condition scan using a case-sensitive contains on the lowercase end tag, so uppercase or mixed-case , , or fails to close a type 1 block, contrary to the spec.

bugs.summary: A later link reference definition replaces the destination and title of an earlier definition with the same case-insensitive label. For example, [ref]: /first followed by [REF]: /second makes [shown][ref] point to /second instead of preserving the first definition.
bugs.match_rule: The report must identify last-definition-wins behavior for duplicate ordinary link reference labels, including case-insensitive duplicates, and attribute the destination/title replacement to reference-definition insertion in the first pass.

bugs.summary: Trailing heading attributes on a setext heading in a definition list truncate at an offset before an already parsed child, inverting a range and panicking.
bugs.match_rule: Names setext heading attribute handling calling truncate_siblings with a cutoff before an existing child, which trips the debug assertion in Tree::truncate_siblings or yields an inverted item range that panics when sliced.
bugs.caveat: The release panic is a real slice panic, not only the debug assertion. Needs both options. Added while building the key, not in the original candidates.

bugs.summary: Code-span edge-space normalization also removes the leading and trailing spaces when the entire payload consists of spaces. The two-space span `  ` therefore produces an empty Code event and empty <code> element instead of preserving both spaces.
bugs.match_rule: The report must identify loss of an all-space inline-code payload caused by make_code_span applying its surrounding-space trimming rule to that payload, such as turning a two-space code span into an empty one.
